races.name: Summer Plate Ladies Day Book Now Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Frisky Whiskey
runners_data.note: Only confirmed pace-setter in field of hold-up horses, gets uncontested lead but must prove stamina at this trip
runners_data.comment: Showed only a glimmer of promise before weakening into sixth on recent bumper debut
runners_data.spotlight: Showed only a glimmer of promise before weakening into well-held sixth on recent bumper debut at Southwell (good); needs to take a good step forward on this hurdling debut.

runners_data.name: Cockney Cleopatra
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits if pace is steady, but two recent pull-ups raise serious reliability concerns for new stable
runners_data.spotlight: Not beaten far when fifth of nine in Clonmel maiden (2m, soft) in November but pulled up twice for new stable at Fontwell this spring (2m3f/2m1f); could be considered only if lively in the betting.

runners_data.name: Bailey's Luck
runners_data.note: Lightly raced type switching to hurdles with hood fitted, completely unexposed over obstacles but bred for this game
runners_data.comment: Well beaten when 200-1 for 1m AW maiden on Flat debut in September; hurdle debut today
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten when 200-1 for 1m AW maiden on Flat debut in September; now switched to hurdling with a hood fitted.

runners_data.name: Aimeric
runners_data.note: Prominent style could be crucial asset in slow-run race, but looked hesitant at hurdles on disappointing debut
runners_data.comment: Smart on the Flat at his best but disappointing on hurdle debut; tricky to weigh up now
runners_data.spotlight: Smart on the Flat at his best but signed off for Karl Burke with two disappointing runs in the autumn and was rather hesitant at some of the flights when disappointing favourite on last month's stable/hurdle debut; subsequently tailed off in major Flat handicap; may yet get his act together over hurdles but he is very tricky to weigh up at the moment.

runners_data.name: Wahraan
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with useful flat form, ran well on hurdle debut but needs strong pace to showcase finishing kick
runners_data.comment: Has the raw ability but is an awkward ride nowadays and comes with risk
runners_data.spotlight: Has some useful Flat form and kept on steadily from a long way off the pace to take third on hurdle debut at Wetherby (2m, soft) in November; subsequent Grade 2 defeat is easily overlooked but he has become a very awkward ride, often refusing to settle and/or hanging; comes with risk.

runners_data.name: Popalot
runners_data.note: Hold-up type coming off disappointing hurdle debut three weeks ago at this course, needs significant improvement
runners_data.comment: Low-key start to hurdling career when well-beaten 40-1 shot here (2m) three weeks ago
runners_data.spotlight: Not disgraced in two course bumpers last season but made low-key start to hurdling career when well beaten at 40-1 here (2m) three weeks ago.

runners_data.name: Prince Abu
runners_data.note: 679 days since last run makes this a complete guessing game despite claiming jockey advantage
runners_data.comment: Both hurdle runs in 2024 were underwhelming; well beaten off basement Flat mark last month
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced since his two very underwhelming hurdle runs for Derek Shaw in summer 2024 and returned from 318-day absence with 19l defeat off basement Flat mark last month; swaps hood for refitted cheekpieces; tongue-tie a first.

runners_data.name: Jessie Jump Jet
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who went close last time at Warwick, shorter trip today should suit tactical speed
runners_data.comment: 0-9 over hurdles but went close in recent Warwick handicap; high on the list
runners_data.spotlight: 0-9 over hurdles but went close in Class 5 handicap at Warwick (2m5f, good) this month and should be fine over today's shorter trip; might have been found a good opportunity.

races.paceDynamic: With only one confirmed front runner in Frisky Whiskey facing seven hold-up/midfield types, this race sets up as a straightforward scenario where the pace-setter gets an easy lead. Frisky Whiskey will dictate terms unchallenged through the early stages, likely creating a sustainable tempo that won't stretch the field. The lack of pace pressure means the race will develop into a sprint finish where horses with tactical speed and the ability to quicken off a steady gallop will have the advantage. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners who can track the leader and hold-up horses with a strong finishing kick.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Frisky Whiskey gets an easy lead and stays on strongly
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace allows Frisky Whiskey to control the race completely, setting up a rhythm that suits his stamina reserves perfectly. Hold-up horses struggle to make up ground when the gallop hasn't been testing enough to set up their finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Kick Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the steady pace sets up a sprint finish in the final furlong
scenarios.body: The uncontested lead creates a moderate gallop that allows closers like Cockney Cleopatra and Wahraan to unleash their finishing speed. Class horses with proven ability get first run and outfinish the pace-setter who has done too much work.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Speed Wins
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent tracker like Aimeric moves to challenge early
scenarios.body: Aimeric uses his flat speed to press Frisky Whiskey from the home turn, creating enough pace to blunt the finishing kicks of the hold-up brigade. The tactical battle between the two most forward runners decides the outcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If the favourites fail to handle the tactical nature
scenarios.body: The steady pace and lack of early positioning pressure allows a lightly-weighted outsider like Jessie Jump Jet or Bailey's Luck to get into contention. The lack of a strong gallop means stamina becomes less important than raw finishing speed.

watchPoints.text: Cockney Cleopatra pulled up twice this spring for new stable and any sign of reluctance in preliminaries would be terminal
Frisky Whiskey has never run beyond 2m before so watch for any signs of emptying in final half-furlong
Aimeric looked hesitant at flights on hurdle debut so monitor jumping technique early doors
Bailey's Luck wearing hood for first time and completely unexposed over hurdles, market moves would be significant
Prince Abu returning after 679-day absence with claiming jockey, any positive pre-race vibes worth noting

races.name: Geoff Handley's Grand 80th Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Livano Bello
runners_data.note: Front-running type who will dictate the pace but faces stronger finishers and carries topweight without recent hurdles success.
runners_data.comment: Didn't fire on latest hurdling start but is largely consistent; chase debut today
runners_data.spotlight: Didn't fire over hurdles at Perth a fortnight ago and is now 0-13 in that sphere but he's generally pretty consistent and will be suited by the trip-and-ground combination on this chasing debut.

runners_data.name: Get A Superstar
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 203-day absence which raises serious fitness concerns despite his placed chasing debut.
runners_data.spotlight: Placed on chasing debut in December 2024 but raced only once last season, when modest seventh in Sedgefield race won by El Muchacho in November; back from another layoff today; current ability is hard to gauge.

runners_data.name: El Muchacho
runners_data.note: Classic closer with proven course and distance form who benefits from claiming jockey's allowance and good ground conditions.
runners_data.comment: Won twice last season and posted another good effort when second over C&D this month
runners_data.spotlight: Won twice on good ground (2m5f/2m3f) for this new stable last season and has been placed on last three appearances, most recently when second over C&D (good) three weeks ago; 1lb lower today and seems very likely to be in the thick of things again.

runners_data.name: Play By The Rules
runners_data.note: Prominent runner carrying bottom weight who showed promise on stable debut and could improve for that Newcastle outing.
runners_data.comment: Made a promising stable debut in March; unlucky to be brought down last time
runners_data.spotlight: Returned from long absence with a promising stable debut at Newcastle (2m4f, good to soft) in March, when he travelled strongly for a long way, and he was unlucky to be brought down fairly early on at Hexham this month; remains well handicapped on old form; might be the answer.

races.paceDynamic: Livano Bello will be the primary pace-setter with both prominent runners likely to track closely behind the early leader. Play By The Rules and Livano Bello should ensure a steady gallop over this extended trip, while El Muchacho and Get A Superstar will need to be positioned to strike from off the pace. The lack of genuine speed horses suggests a moderate tempo that will quicken from the final fence. This race shape clearly favours hold-up horses who can produce late kicks, as the pace won't be strong enough to blunt closing finishes.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace remains moderate as expected
scenarios.body: The steady gallop will suit El Muchacho and Get A Superstar perfectly, allowing them to conserve energy before unleashing finishing kicks. Both closers have the class edge over the pace-setters in a sprint finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Livano Bello Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Livano Bello gets an easy lead and dictates terms
scenarios.body: The front-runner can use his stamina to stretch the field from three out, potentially getting first run on his rivals. His consistency gives him every chance if not pressured early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Battle Unfolds
scenarios.trigger: If Play By The Rules and Livano Bello engage in early pace pressure
scenarios.body: The dual prominent runners push each other along, creating a stronger gallop that sets up the race perfectly for the hold-up pair. El Muchacho's class tells in a slowly-run finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If all runners go steady and it becomes a sprint
scenarios.body: The race turns into a pure stamina test where fitness and recent form becomes crucial. Play By The Rules could benefit from his recent promising Newcastle run.

watchPoints.text: Get A Superstar's fitness after 203 days off could see him fade quickly despite his hold-up style suiting the race shape.
Livano Bello needs to avoid early pressure from Play By The Rules to maintain his front-running advantage.
El Muchacho's recent second over course and distance makes him the form horse but he must overcome topweight.
Play By The Rules showed promise last time but needs to prove his stamina over this extended trip.
William Maggs' 3lb claim for El Muchacho effectively drops him below the other topweight Livano Bello.

races.name: Family Extravaganza Raceday On Sunday 5th July Mares' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Cher Tara
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who needs everything to fall right from her backmarker style but has shown glimpses of ability on good ground
runners_data.comment: Didn't run badly at Kelso this month but has modest strike-rate; others appeal more
runners_data.spotlight: Didn't run badly when fifth of eight at Kelso (2m5f, good) three weeks ago and continues to slip down the weights but has modest 2-21 strike-rate over hurdles; others appeal more.

runners_data.name: Lone Star
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in ideal conditions with course and distance win under his belt, though trainer out of form recently
runners_data.comment: C&D winner last spring but nothing like the force of old and has become inconsistent
runners_data.spotlight: Capitalised upon some considerable help from the handicapper when winning over C&D (good) just under a year ago and returns here after a decent effort at Kelso this month, but she's nothing like the force of old and has become inconsistent.

runners_data.name: Royal Maggs
runners_data.note: Prominent but has tendency to fade in finish which is concerning over this stamina test
runners_data.comment: Not beaten far in her first two handicaps (2m7f/2m5f) but needs improvement
runners_data.spotlight: Last of four when upped to 2m7f for last month's handicap debut and only eighth of ten (behind Lone Star) when dropped back to 2m5f at Kelso three weeks ago; not beaten far in either of those races but needs to up her game; usual hood is left off.

runners_data.name: Little Soiree
runners_data.note: Prominent racer now 20lb lower than her last win but form has completely collapsed in recent months
runners_data.comment: Has badly lost her way since winning for another stable last spring
runners_data.spotlight: Now 20lb lower than when winning over 2m for Chris Gordon just over a year ago but has badly lost her way; huge leap of faith is required to support her.

runners_data.name: Mistral Blue
runners_data.note: Likely pace-setter who has won twice over similar trips on good ground and returns from encouraging seasonal reappearance
runners_data.comment: Returned from break with a quite encouraging run this month; enters calculations
runners_data.spotlight: Dual 2m3f hurdle winner on good ground; pulled up on soft at end of last year but returned from a break with a quite encouraging fifth of 12 at Warwick (2m5f, good) this month and enters calculations here.

runners_data.name: Time Was
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare returning after 93-day break but was consistent before and has strong course form
runners_data.comment: 0-19 under rules but in the frame all four starts since clear C&D second in November
runners_data.spotlight: 0-19 under rules but returned from a break with a clear second over C&D (good to soft) in November and made the frame on all three subsequent appearances; returns from another break today; can make her presence felt.

runners_data.name: Parish Star
runners_data.note: Hold-up tactician with good recent form for new yard and proven on this ground despite trainer success
runners_data.comment: 2-5 for new stable this year; good third at Kelso last month; likely contender again
runners_data.spotlight: 2-5 for new stable this year; gained the wins on heavy and good to soft ground but coped perfectly well with good ground when close third at Kelso (2m5f; first-time tongue-tie) last month; hood (worn for three of her last four races) is discarded; likely contender again.

runners_data.name: Lady Fortune
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with first-time hood after wind surgery but poor hurdle record and long absence are major concerns
runners_data.comment: Pulled up on stable debut but the ground was soft; had wind op since; worth market check
runners_data.spotlight: Unplaced all six hurdle runs, most recently when pulled up in soft-ground handicap on stable debut in January; combination of wind surgery, first-time hood and return to good ground could plausibly prompt a better performance here, though; worth a glance in the betting.

races.paceDynamic: Mistral Blue looks the only natural front runner and should set a comfortable rhythm from the start with Lone Star, Royal Maggs and Little Soiree tracking in prominent positions. The pace will be moderate rather than searching, as none of the prominent racers are confirmed tearaways, allowing the race to develop into a test of stamina over the final 4f. With half the field adopting hold-up tactics (Cher Tara, Time Was, Parish Star, Lady Fortune), this should create a bunched finish where horses need to be produced with well-timed challenges. This shape strongly favours prominent racers who can secure good positions early and avoid the scrimmaging that hold-up horses will face.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Racers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Mistral Blue sets a steady tempo and the prominent group maintain their positions
scenarios.body: The pace will be honest but not punishing, allowing Lone Star and Mistral Blue to kick clear in the final 2f before the hold-up brigade can mount their challenges. Royal Maggs could also benefit if she doesn't fade as badly as recent form suggests.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Challenge Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes too slow and bunches the field
scenarios.body: Parish Star and Cher Tara will get the perfect setup to unleash finishing kicks, with Time Was also dangerous despite her long absence. The prominent racers will be sitting ducks if they've been going too slowly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If Mistral Blue doesn't lead or gets headed early by prominent racers
scenarios.body: Little Soiree or Royal Maggs could steal a march by going forward when the expected pace scenario breaks down. This would create a muddling race where tactical speed matters more than pure stamina.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Ambush
scenarios.trigger: If the favourite types underperform and the pace becomes tactical
scenarios.body: Lady Fortune could spring a surprise off her low weight despite poor recent form, or Time Was could capitalise on others' mistakes after her lengthy break. The combination of light weights and tactical positioning could prove decisive.

watchPoints.text: Mistral Blue's jumping early on as she's likely to dictate and any mistakes could disrupt the entire pace scenario
Little Soiree's position through the race as her recent form suggests she may not handle the prominent role her style suggests
Time Was for ring-rustiness signs after 93 days off despite her decent course record
Royal Maggs for any signs of her finishing fade developing before the final 2f
Parish Star's positioning turning in as she'll need clear room to deliver her customary late challenge

races.name: Anji Fletcher Memorial Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Snatch A Glance
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with solid recent form who should get a good pitch tracking Jackstell early on
runners_data.comment: 2m Ludlow novice winner; up in trip for handicap debut; should have more to offer
runners_data.spotlight: Just did enough to win 2m Ludlow maiden in the autumn and was a very respectable third of six in novice event over that C&D (again on good) last month; moves up in trip for handicap debut; should have more to offer.

runners_data.name: Crebilly
runners_data.note: Quality hold-up performer but well below his best recently and faces a tactical disadvantage from the back
runners_data.comment: Well below best during light campaign last season but has slipped to a dangerous mark
runners_data.spotlight: Very useful hurdler/chaser in his prime; well below best during a fairly light campaign last season (four hurdle runs; cheekpieces added last time) but will appreciate this ease in grade and has slipped to a dangerous mark.

runners_data.name: Jackstell
runners_data.note: Front runner returning from 178-day break who should get the easy lead he needs to be effective
runners_data.spotlight: Won three consecutive small-field races in the autumn, the latest a Plumpton handicap (2m4f, good); absent since struggling on soft ground there in December but remains lightly raced and could plausibly still have more improvement to come.

runners_data.name: High Dancer
runners_data.note: Prominent type with stamina questions over longer trips but this distance should suit better
runners_data.comment: Didn't see out 3m last time but still ran well; big player if aided by new cheekpieces
runners_data.spotlight: Didn't see out 3m when well-held third at Doncaster (good to soft) in March but ran well for a long way and is now back on same mark as for his clear second behind a useful rival there (2m3f, soft) in November; also suited by good ground; could be a tough nut to crack if aided by new cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Sun Art
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in good current form who needs a strong pace to close into
runners_data.comment: Second off this mark at Hereford (2m) last month and worth another crack at this trip
runners_data.spotlight: Yet to make any further progress since winning a 2m Ludlow novice in March 2025 but posted a sound effort when second off today's mark at Hereford (2m, good) last month and is work another crack at this sort of trip.

runners_data.name: Nitty Gritty
runners_data.note: Bottom weight closer with cheekpieces fitted who has mixed form but recent Kelso second was encouraging
runners_data.comment: Has a mixed record for this stable (since the autumn) but ran well when second this month
runners_data.spotlight: 0-7 for current stable (since the autumn) and has a very mixed record but ran well when second in refitted cheekpieces at Kelso (2m5f, good) this month and was unlucky to come to grief at Uttoxeter recently; remains on a good mark; can't be ruled out.

runners_data.name: Lord Chamberlain
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who won easily last time but struggled under penalty and faces stronger opposition here
runners_data.comment: Won easily on last month's handicap debut (2m); held under penalty since; still considered
runners_data.spotlight: Displayed considerable improvement when winning easily by 12l on last month's handicap hurdle debut at Hereford (2m, good); managed only third under 7lb penalty here (2m2f, good) eight days later and is another 5lb higher today, but he moves up in trip again and remains of interest.

races.paceDynamic: Jackstell is the only confirmed front runner in this small field and should get an uncontested lead, setting a sustainable rhythm over this staying trip. High Dancer and Snatch A Glance will likely track him prominently, with the hold-up quartet of Crebilly, Sun Art, Nitty Gritty and Lord Chamberlain settling further back. The moderate early pace will allow Jackstell to dictate terms without pressure, making it difficult for closers to bridge the gap in the straight. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and front runners who can capitalise on the soft fractions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jackstell Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Jackstell gets the easy lead he expects and maintains his rhythm
scenarios.body: The front runner faces no early pressure and kicks clear turning in, making it very hard for the hold-up horses to close the gap. His three autumn wins all came from prominent positions and this tactical advantage should prove decisive.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pressure Tells
scenarios.trigger: If High Dancer or Snatch A Glance press Jackstell from early stages
scenarios.body: The increased pace softens up Jackstell but also stretches the field, favouring those who can travel strongly in behind the leaders. High Dancer's stamina questions are negated by the shorter trip while Snatch A Glance gets her preferred aggressive tempo.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace allows the back markers to close dramatically in the final furlong. Sun Art and Lord Chamberlain have both shown smart finishing kicks when conditions suit their patient tactics.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Experience Counts
scenarios.trigger: If Crebilly's class advantage overcomes his recent poor form
scenarios.body: The veteran's superior ability shines through despite tactical disadvantages, potentially aided by Harry Cobden's strength in the saddle. His hold-up style works if others go too hard too early.

watchPoints.text: Jackstell must break alertly to secure the uncontested lead his front-running style demands
High Dancer and Snatch A Glance could disrupt the pace if either decides to press Jackstell early
Crebilly's jumping under pressure given his recent struggles and long absence from winning form
Lord Chamberlain's ability to settle given his tendency to get keen and waste energy
The pace through the middle sections which will determine if closers can get competitive

races.name: Dine In The Altior's Resturant Novices' Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Catchim
runners_data.note: Front-running specialist who won over course and distance last month by leading throughout, perfectly suited to dictate terms here
runners_data.comment: Left clear after final fence to score over C&D last month; 4lb rise not excessive
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner who was left clear just after final fence to score over C&D (good) last month, opening his chase account at the 12th attempt; evidently in good nick and subsequent 4lb rise is not excessive.

runners_data.name: Lheur De Gloire
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning from wind surgery with promise but needs strong early pace to be effective from the back
runners_data.comment: 0-5 over hurdles but shaped well on latest outing; interesting on chase debut
runners_data.spotlight: 0-5 over hurdles but shaped well before fading into fourth of 13 at Southwell (2m, good; first run after wind op) this month and Ben Pauling is evidently keen to launch his chasing career; interesting.

runners_data.name: Cawthorne Cracker
runners_data.note: Patient hold-up style hampered by poor recent form and 0-6 record over fences despite decent course third last month
runners_data.comment: Below form at Stratford recently but was placed over C&D last month; a possible
runners_data.spotlight: Not at his best at Stratford 11 days ago and now 0-6 over fences but he had returned from a break with a pretty good third over C&D (good) last month and his current mark is workable.

runners_data.name: Walk The Plank
runners_data.note: Hold-up tactician with modest form but showed battling qualities when winning at Huntingdon, needs race to develop late
runners_data.comment: Form of his hard-fought Huntingdon win looks modest but further progress is possible
runners_data.spotlight: Battled well for narrow success at Huntingdon (2m, good) in March, his third start over fences; that form looks modest and he's 4lb higher here but further progress is possible.

runners_data.name: Intenzo
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose clear second at Sedgefield demonstrates tactical speed but three poor efforts since raise questions
runners_data.comment: Good second on chase/handicap debut in March but three lesser efforts have followed
runners_data.spotlight: Made a promising chase/handicap debut when clear second at Sedgefield (2m, good; form well advertised by winner since) in March but three lesser efforts have followed and his tendency to race too freely remains a worry.

races.paceDynamic: Catchim will lead from the front as the sole confirmed pace-setter, with Intenzo likely tracking him prominently. The remaining three runners (Lheur De Gloire, Cawthorne Cracker, Walk The Plank) all prefer hold-up tactics, creating a split field dynamic. With no pressure on Catchim early, he can dictate a sustainable tempo and kick clear approaching the final fence as he did when winning here last month. This race shape strongly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can avoid getting caught behind the hold-up brigade.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Catchim Leads Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Catchim settles and jumps cleanly in front without early pressure.
scenarios.body: He can replicate his course win by dictating terms and kicking clear approaching the final fence when the hold-up horses are still gathering momentum. His proven course form and sustainable front-running style makes him ideally suited to exploit this tactical setup.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Intenzo tracks Catchim closely and times his challenge perfectly.
scenarios.body: The promising chaser can use his prominent style to shadow the leader and strike in the final furlong when Catchim's stamina wavers. His clear second at Sedgefield shows he has the tactical speed to capitalize on favorable positioning.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Charge Success
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses early and the hold-up horses get perfect splits.
scenarios.body: Walk The Plank or Cawthorne Cracker could benefit from their patient tactics if they find clear runs and the leaders come back to them. However, both need everything to fall right given their inferior recent form.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Lheur Victory
scenarios.trigger: If Lheur De Gloire's wind operation has transformed him completely.
scenarios.body: The Ben Pauling runner showed promise before fading at Southwell and could surprise if fully effective after his recent procedure. His hold-up style needs a strong pace collapse to be effective in this tactical setup.

watchPoints.text: Catchim must settle early and not get keen in front as any rushing could compromise his stamina reserves
Intenzo's jumping under pressure given three disappointing efforts since his promising debut second at Sedgefield
Walk The Plank's fitness after 71-day break and whether he can reproduce his Huntingdon battling qualities
Lheur De Gloire's wind operation effectiveness as he faded badly before the procedure at Southwell
The pace through the early stages as all hold-up horses need a strong gallop to be competitive

races.name: Half Year Annual Badges On Sale Now Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Iolaos Du Mou
runners_data.note: Non-runner despite being listed as the main pace angle
runners_data.comment: Won in this month last year and returned from layoff with an encouraging run 24 days ago
runners_data.spotlight: Just held on to make all at Warwick in this month last year and returned from layoff with encouraging sixth of 16 at Uttoxeter 26 days ago, weakening out of contention in only the closing stages; no surprise if he gives this a good shot.

runners_data.name: Ruler Legend
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with excellent course form having won twice here this season on good ground
runners_data.comment: Ended last season in excellent form, winning twice here (2m/2m2f); big chance
runners_data.spotlight: Ended last season in excellent form, winning twice here (2m/2m2f) on good ground, and is probably still on a workable mark; big chance.

runners_data.name: Assorda
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who needs strong pace to show her best but has limited winning form since debut success
runners_data.comment: Soundly beaten on all four starts for new stable this year (2m1f-2m4f)
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-French mare; fortunate to win small-field Catterick novice (1m7f, good) for Paula Smith on British debut in March 2025 and soundly beaten in all five subsequent handicaps, the last four times for new stable this year; drops back in trip (from 2m4f).

runners_data.name: Bunker Bay
runners_data.note: Hold-up type reported to have had breathing issues last time and seeking first hurdle win in ten attempts
runners_data.comment: Clear second to Ruler Legend over C&D last month; had a breathing issue on latest outing
runners_data.spotlight: Reportedly had breathing issue when well beaten at Perth last month and is now 0-9 over hurdles but his clear second to next-time-out winner Ruler Legend over C&D (good) two starts ago was a good effort; big player if back at that level.

runners_data.name: Paragon
runners_data.note: Prominent runner still seeking first win over hurdles but showed encouragement in handicap debut
runners_data.comment: Made fairly encouraging handicap hurdle debut this month; refitted cheekpieces might help
runners_data.spotlight: 0-11 on the Flat and 0-4 over hurdles; made a fairly encouraging handicap hurdle debut when sixth of 13 at Southwell (2m, good) this month, though, and might be boosted by refitted cheekpieces here.

runners_data.name: Made All
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who finished strongly for third over course and distance on handicap debut three weeks ago
runners_data.comment: Given a lot to do before finishing well for third over C&D on handicap hurdle debut
runners_data.spotlight: Fair Flat racer; yet to make a significant impact over hurdles but was given a lot to do before finishing well for third over C&D (good) on handicap debut three weeks ago, and his recent Flat run was perfectly respectable.

runners_data.name: Red Trail
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning from long absence but was placed in this race last year at huge odds
runners_data.spotlight: Belied 80-1 odds when placed off today's mark in this race last year but was well beaten on next hurdling start and has been absent since some disappointing Flat runs in the autumn; too risky.

runners_data.name: Melosa
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who was pulled up on hurdle debut here and drops back in trip today
runners_data.comment: Pulled up when 100-1 for last month's handicap hurdle debut; drops back from 2m4f
runners_data.spotlight: Showed some ability on the Flat but was pulled up when 100-1 for handicap hurdle debut here (2m4f, good) in April; drops back in trip today; can't be recommended.

races.paceDynamic: Iolaos Du Mou is marked as a non-runner but was the only confirmed front-runner, leaving Ruler Legend and Paragon as the most likely pace-setters from their prominent styles. With six hold-up horses in an 8-runner field, the early pace will be modest as Ruler Legend and Paragon won't need to work hard to establish position. The race will develop into a tactical affair with plenty of horse left for the final half-mile, creating a scenario where patient tactics and finishing kick matter most. This shape heavily favours hold-up horses who can produce late acceleration.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is modest as expected with limited pressure on the leaders
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the final half-mile where patient tactics prevail. Late-running horses with finishing speed can pick off the early leaders who've had an easy time of it.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Ruler Legend Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Ruler Legend uses his course form to dictate from the front without serious challenge
scenarios.body: His two wins here this season give him tactical advantage and he can time his effort perfectly. The prominent runner gets first run on the hold-up brigade.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Finish
scenarios.trigger: If both Ruler Legend and Paragon go too slowly and get caught napping
scenarios.body: The race turns into a messy scramble where positioning becomes crucial and the best-positioned horse wins. Experience and racecraft decide the outcome rather than pure ability.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Early Burn-Up
scenarios.trigger: If Ruler Legend and Paragon engage in an unexpected pace duel from early
scenarios.body: Both prominent runners compromise their chances by going too fast too soon. Any horse with tactical speed from mid-division can capitalize on their mistakes.

watchPoints.text: Ruler Legend's early positioning will dictate the entire race shape given his prominent style and course advantage
Made All's finishing kick from three weeks ago suggests he could be very dangerous if getting the right tactical setup
Bunker Bay needs monitoring for any breathing equipment changes after reported issues at Perth last month
The absence of Iolaos Du Mou removes the main pace pressure and makes this more tactical than expected
Red Trail's fitness after 342-day absence will show early if he's ready to reproduce last year's surprise placing effort
